batchName: Early Republic: The Samnite Wars (367-290 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Early Republic: The Samnite Wars (367-290 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: At the Caudine Forks the Romans walked under the iugum. What was it?
questions.explanation: Passing under the yoke showed that an army had been defeated and subjugated.
questions.sourceQuote: The Romans filed out unarmed under the yoke (*iugum*), a frame of spears

questions.question: What was the devotio of Publius Decius Mus at Sentinum?
options: He offered his own life to the gods and charged the enemy
He made peace with the Gauls
questions.explanation: His sacrifice rallied his men, and the coalition collapsed.
questions.sourceQuote: Decius then devoted himself (*devotio*): he prayed to the gods

questions.question: Who were Rome’s socii?
options: Its allies, who sent soldiers for its wars
questions.explanation: Allied peoples kept their own governments but sent troops at their own expense.
questions.sourceQuote: Allied peoples, the *socii* ("allies"), kept their own governments,

questions.question: What was a deditio, like Capua’s surrender in Livy’s story?
questions.explanation: By surrendering, Campania became Roman property that Rome had to defend.

questions.question: What did the title pro consule mean?
questions.explanation: Commanders whose command was extended to finish a campaign became proconsuls.
questions.sourceQuote: with the title of proconsul (*pro consule*, "in place of a consul").

questions.question: At Aquilonia, what was the legio linteata?
options: The Linen Legion of Samnites sworn never to flee
questions.explanation: Elite Samnite units swore a sacred oath never to flee, on pain of death.
questions.sourceQuote: Elite units, the Linen Legion (*legio linteata*), swore a sacred oath

questions.question: The Samnites were forced into a foedus iniquum. What was it?
questions.explanation: After 290 BC the Samnites had to ally with Rome on Rome’s terms.
questions.sourceQuote: on unequal terms (*foedus iniquum*, an "unequal treaty").

questions.question: Fabius’s brother crossed the silva Ciminia. What was it?
options: The Ciminian Forest, which no Roman had crossed
questions.explanation: He crossed it disguised as a shepherd, and Fabius then led his army through it.
questions.sourceQuote: through the dreaded Ciminian Forest (*silva Ciminia*), which no Roman had ever crossed.
